text: For two solutions y₁, y₂ of a second-order linear homogeneous ODE, the ___ W = y₁y₂' − y₂y₁' vanishes identically if and only if the solutions are linearly dependent.
explanation: The Wronskian W(y₁, y₂) = y₁y₂' − y₂y₁' detects linear dependence: by Abel's theorem it satisfies W' = −P(x)W, so it is either identically zero (dependent solutions) or nowhere zero (independent). It also appears in the variation-of-parameters formula for the particular solution of an inhomogeneous linear ODE.
